hook_weights.name: Multi-post product launch arc (mystery teaser → reveal → date-lock + countdown — 3+ sequenced posts over 5-7 days)

provenance.note: WITHIN-45d GAP CLOSED (no weight change). EP-017 (UGC 'real reviews' social-proof post, IG 6.96% ER / NCS 100, FB NCS 89) is explicitly a post-date-lock LAUNCH-TAIL beat of the HW-019 launch arc, pairing with the already-linked EP-014 winner-announcement beat. Refined onto the existing arc entry rather than added as a near-duplicate hook: the arc is the mechanism, the UGC review post is an approved tail beat that replaces stale 'it's here' reposts.

rules: Minimum 3 posts over a 5-7 day arc with narrative escalation: (1) mystery + drop date implied, (2) visual reveal + product name implied, (3) named product + explicit date-lock + scarcity.
Always include a LinkedIn image+copy beat in the launch arc (SYN-20260531).
Giveaway/sweepstakes mechanics amplify only INSIDE the arc — never as decontextualized standalone blasts (EP-013).
After the date-lock, extend the arc with PARTICIPATION beats (hide -> hunt -> winner announcement with live scarcity count) — never another 'it's here' repost (EP-014, 2nd-cycle).
hook_weights.notes: Performance Memory SYN-20260522 (NEW CP-015): Golden Pear launch arc — 9 posts across IG/FB/TT/LinkedIn over May 1-6, 4 of 9 hit NCS 100. FB Reel step 2 ("New look. New flavor. New obsession. Coming soon.") = 41,043 imp / 3,148 eng / 7.67% ER / NCS 100 — largest single-post FB engagement event since CP-010 Ashton Hall. IG step 3 ("Some of you guessed it. Golden Pear is here. May 13th.") = 21,105 imp / 712 eng / 3.37% / NCS 100. LinkedIn launch teaser hit 11.11% engagement (n=1). The teaser ALONE is weak (EP-010 stayed LOW confidence last cycle); the FULL ARC is what crosses NCS 100. **Cross-platform (IG/FB/TT/LinkedIn). HIGH confidence — 9-post validation across 4 platforms.** Promotes EP-010 to confirmed CP-015. Template for Larry: minimum 3 posts, 5-7 day arc, narrative escalation = (1) mystery + drop date implied, (2) visual reveal + product name implied, (3) named product + explicit date-lock + scarcity ("limited run"). Test on next flavor drop and next product launch. **UPDATE SYN-20260531: arc CONFIRMED on LinkedIn — Golden Pear sweepstakes posts drove LI new-window median to 18.22% (n=5), incl. 'Day 2 of the Golden Pear Sweepstakes' 36.65% and 'To every mom…' 35.64%. Always include a LinkedIn image+copy beat in the launch arc. CAVEAT (EP-013): the sweepstakes mechanic only amplifies INSIDE the arc — standalone 'WANT TO WIN BIG' reposts landed NCS 7-23. Frame giveaways as part of the launch narrative, never as decontextualized blasts. UPDATE SYN-20260612 (EP-014 → MEDIUM, 2nd-cycle validation): after the date-lock, extend the arc with PARTICIPATION beats — hide → hunt → winner announcement with live scarcity count ('We have our first winner… 4 still out there') hit FB 5.98% / NCS 97.3 and IG 3.08% / NCS 99.2 — never another 'it's here' repost (this window's boosted flavor-drop reposts ran 191K/42K/34K imp at 0.35–1.34% ER).**

The 2026-07-18 pickleball cluster extends it cross-platform on a single shared concept: FB reel NCS 56.4 (2.83% ER / 424 imp, ~3.3x the AP-010-depressed 0.87% FB median), IG reel NCS 28.7 (5.61% ER / 659 imp, ~2.0x the 2.83% IG median), LinkedIn NCS 34.7 (7.45% ER / 188 imp — well BELOW the 26.56% LI median, falsified on LI). Weight set conservatively at 1.2 (mild lift, LOW confidence): the ER multiples are real but reach was small on every surface and the FB comparison rides on an artificially depressed median. This is the THIRD pattern confirming the LinkedIn register rule — LI accepts institutional/science/community framing (CP-009, EP-019) and rejects consumer-lifestyle/individual framing (EP-018, EP-001-sport).

hook_weights.name: Cause-campaign stake-first lede (origin story or gratitude first, ask last)
hook_weights.example: The Leadville Trail 100 started for one reason: to keep Leadville alive. The Willow Fire is testing the town again, so we're doing what the race was built to do. [...] Stock your training block. Fund the comeback.
rules: Open with the STAKE (why this place/cause matters, what is at risk) or with GRATITUDE (what it gave us). Never open with the ask.
Keep the commerce mechanic - it does not depress performance when it sits at the end. Close terse: 'Stock your training block. Fund the comeback.'
Do NOT open with 'Help us raise $X' / 'Time to give back' + mechanic. Those two ledes were the bottom two performers on the identical offer.
Scoped facebook/instagram. NOT LinkedIn: LI showed 7.81% (gratitude) vs 6.99% (ask-first), effectively flat at n=1 each - the lede effect did not reproduce there.
MEDIUM confidence: n=11 posts but ONE campaign. Confirm on the next cause/relief moment before promoting to a confirmed CP.
hook_weights.notes: Performance Memory SYN-20260813-001 (NEW EP-020), window 2026-07-19..2026-07-30. Refines EP-015 (HW-020), which was derived from Memorial Day where the winning variants happened to have no CTA at all. Leadville separates the two variables: offer held constant, lede varied. The FB stake-first post was the single largest organic event of the window at 23,395 imp / 1,752 eng / 7.49% ER - 25x the FB window median. Caveat: paid_status reads organic_only on all 56 queue posts, and paid linkage is known-unreliable upstream (content_links unpopulated in paid-media-state.json), so the 23K reach warrants a paid-linkage spot-check before it is treated as a pure-organic benchmark.

provenance.note: NEW EP-020. Cause-campaign lede ordering, isolated on a single offer. The Leadville/Willow Fire campaign ran ONE identical mechanic (10% of every order + Kenetik dollar-for-dollar match up to $100,000) across 11 posts with five different opening framings, same week, same accounts. Weighted ER by lede: stake-first origin story 7.43% (23,747 imp) > gratitude-first 4.99% > slogan+mechanic 3.08% > ask-first 1.95%. Facebook-controlled: 7.49% (23,395 imp) vs 1.34% (449 imp) = 5.6x. Instagram-controlled: 4.69-5.56% vs 1.70% = 2.8-3.3x. This SHARPENS EP-015: the commerce CTA is not what kills a cause post - putting the ask in the LEDE is. EP-015's rule (drop the CTA on solemn moments) forfeits revenue; this one keeps the mechanic and moves it to the last line.

After three consecutive zero-post windows, one YouTube cross-post landed on 2026-07-24T19:25:27Z (the Leadville stage-race body, cross-posted from IG/TT) and returned 0 impressions / 1 engagement - exactly the outcome AP-006 predicts, on its 6th confirmation. anti_patterns.name: Same-day giveaway variant saturation (>1 variant of same offer per platform per day)

provenance.note: BOUNDARY CONDITION REFINED (no multiplier change). EP-012 (athlete-event giveaway CLOSURE / winner-announcement posts hitting NCS 100 at 2.7-3.9k imp on Instagram) is the explicit counter-case to this anti-pattern: the 0.62x penalty applies to same-day duplicate ENTRY variants of one offer, NOT to closure/winner beats, which are a distinct lifecycle moment and outperform the original entry post. Linking EP-012 here (rather than opening a new hook) records the exception on the rule it qualifies.

rules: Max 1 giveaway-mechanic post per platform per day; stagger variants 24-48h apart.

anti_patterns.name: Automated bulk-publish of identical retail/PR copy on Facebook (>1 identical body per platform per day, same-second cluster)

provenance.note: RECONFIRMED 6th CYCLE AND GROWING (multiplier already floored at 0.0). SYN-20260731: 15 'Find Kenetik at QuikTrip!' FB posts all at ER<0.5%, SIX boosted to 166,060 / 119,812 / 62,873 / 54,134 / 31,589 / 20,130 imp at 0.19-0.42% ER against ad 'video__roman quik trip announce__store locator' in campaign 'awareness__quicktrip geo target__cbo' — paid amplification on dead retail copy is now LARGER than the prior cycle (6 boosted vs 2), and the retailer rotated Dierbergs->QuikTrip. The same mechanic also hit an EDITORIAL hook for the first time (EP-016 published 40x as same-second FB-reel clones, ~16 at NCS<25 / 0 imp), which is why AP-008 and EP-016 are linked here. The dedupe-per-day + block-paid-boost-on-NCS<25 gate remains UNSHIPPED after six logged cycles: re-escalate P0 to Devon. Counter-signal worth recording: the 2026-07-18 SYN-20260802 window was CLEAN — 6 posts, 6 distinct bodies, no same-second clusters, no paid boost on dead copy — but n=6 on a single day is far too small to read as a fix.

RECONFIRMED 7th CYCLE. The SYN-20260802 'first clean window in 7 cycles' is now CONFIRMED to have been a sample artifact, exactly as flagged at the time (n=6, one day). This window: the EP-016 'Three o'clock and the doc you opened at noon is still blank' body was published 13 times on Facebook in three same-second bursts - 4 copies at 2026-07-22T04:14:33Z, 3 at 04:14:34Z, 3 at 2026-07-23T17:44:38Z. 8 of the 13 returned ZERO engagement. 13 of 26 Facebook posts in the window (50%) were this one body. FB median 0.88% with the clones vs 1.39% without - the flood cuts the FB median by 37%. One copy captured 2,989 of the cluster's 4,107 impressions; the other twelve split 1,118 between them. MEASUREMENT FINDING attached to this entry: the queue UNDERCOUNTS this anti-pattern. Sprout returned 63 posts for the window; published-posts.json holds 56, and all 7 missing posts have zero impressions or no metrics object. The sync (executive-bi-process-task-2a) appears to filter posts lacking impression data - which is precisely the AP-010 signal. Every AP-010 severity count on record is therefore a FLOOR, not a true count. Dedupe-per-day + block-paid-boost-on-NCS<25 gate remains UNSHIPPED after seven logged cycles.

rules: Deduplicate post bodies per-platform per-day BEFORE publish; cap same-body variants at 1/24h (extends the AP-007 rule to body text).
Identify and disable the auto-poster producing same-second clusters — FB spam detection suppresses entire batches (most severe FB anti-pattern in the program).

anti_patterns.name: Amazon / PDP listing text published as an organic social caption (TikTok, Facebook)
